name: Massachusetts

ma-c54-140.citation: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 140 (senators and representatives in congress; vacancies)

ma-c54-141.citation: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 141 (representatives in general court; vacancies)

ma-c54-142.citation: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 142 (district attorneys and county officers)

ma-c54-147.citation: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 147 (elections to fill vacancies)

ma-c53-53.citation: M.G.L. c. 53, s. 53 (vacancies caused by ties; filling)

ma-const.citation: Constitution of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, Amendments Arts. XIV and XVI

ties.applies_to: a state primary (and a city or town primary under chapter 53) when the tie is for the last nomination(s) available
ties.steps: if the number of persons receiving equal votes exceeds the number of nominations available there is deemed to be a vacancy; for an office filled by all the voters of the commonwealth the state committee fills it, for any other office the members of the ward and town committees in the district fill it; the choice must be one of the candidates who received the tie vote
ties.who: the state committee (statewide offices) or the ward and town committees of the district (other offices) of the party

sources.quote: In case of a tie vote where the number of persons receiving equal votes exceeds the number of nominations available, there shall be deemed to be a vacancy.
All vacancies caused by ties shall be filled only by the choice of one of the candidates receiving the tie vote.

ties.note: M.G.L. c. 53, s. 53. Chapter 53 s. 85 and s. 81 (tie votes at caucuses) are about caucuses and were not treated as primaries.

ties.applies_to: U.S. Senator and Representative in Congress, in the biennial state election
ties.steps: upon failure to choose a senator or representative in congress, the governor causes precepts to be issued to the aldermen and selectmen of the district calling an election on a day 145 to 160 days after the failure; the governor appoints a temporary senator until the election (c. 54 s. 140(a), (f))
ties.who: the governor issues the precepts; the voters of the district elect

sources.quote: Upon failure to choose a senator or representative in congress or upon creation of a vacancy in that office, the governor shall immediately cause precepts to be issued to the aldermen in every city and the selectmen in every town in the district, directing them to call an election on the day appointed in the precepts for the election of such senator or representative.

ties.note: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 140. The section says "failure to choose" and never uses the word tie; that a tie is a failure to choose is a reading [inferred]. The word tie does not appear in c. 54 ss. 115, 116, 134, 135, 135B, 137, 138, 140, 141, 142, 147 and 150 as read (those sections were searched for it).

ties.applies_to: State Representative (general court), in the biennial state election
ties.steps: upon failure to elect, the speaker of the house issues precepts to the aldermen and selectmen of the district appointing such time as the house of representatives may order for an election; the election is held on a Tuesday
ties.who: the speaker issues the precepts at the time the House orders; the voters of the district elect

sources.quote: Upon a vacancy in the office of representative in the general court or upon failure to elect, the speaker of the house of representatives shall issue precepts to the aldermen of each city and the selectmen of each town comprising the district or any part thereof, appointing such time as the house of representatives may order for an election to fill such vacancy

ties.note: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 141; "failure to elect" read as including a tie [inferred]. Section 147 adds that at elections held because of a failure to elect the proceedings are the same, so far as applicable, as at the biennial state election. For State Senator no matching section was found in chapter 54 as read (the Constitution makes the senate the final judge of its members' elections; that text was not quoted).

ties.steps: no statutory tie or failure-to-elect provision for state senators was found
ties.note: Read: c. 54 ss. 115, 116, 137, 138, 140, 141, 142, 147, 150 and the table of contents of chapters 53 and 54 (ss. 143 to 146 and 148 to 149 were not fetched). The Constitution (Part the Second, ch. I, sec. II, art. IV) makes the senate the final judge of the elections of its own members; its text is bracketed and amended in the Constitution page and was not relied on.

ties.applies_to: county offices elected at the state election: district attorney, clerk of the courts, register of probate, sheriff
ties.steps: upon failure to choose one of these officers the governor causes precepts to be issued directing an election on the day appointed in them
ties.who: the governor issues the precepts; the voters elect

sources.quote: Upon failure to choose a district attorney, clerk of the courts or in Suffolk county of the supreme judicial or superior court, register of probate or sheriff, the governor shall cause precepts to be issued to the proper officers, directing them to call an election on the day appointed therein for the election of such officer.

ties.note: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 142; "failure to choose" read as including a tie [inferred]. City and town offices are governed by city charters and chapter 43 and town by-laws, which were not read; chapter 54 s. 137 only says the city clerk declares the result after any recount.

ties.applies_to: Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Councillors and the other officers chosen by the voters under the Constitution
ties.steps: the Constitution declares elected the person having the highest number of votes (Amendments, Art. XIV); where there is no election of the governor, lieutenant governor or councillors the legislature fills the office in the manner the Constitution provides for the choice of such officers (Amendments, Art. XVI); a tie is not named
ties.who: the general court (senate and house of representatives)

sources.quote: In all elections of civil officers by the people of this commonwealth, whose election is provided for by the constitution, the person having the highest number of votes shall be deemed and declared to be elected.
but in case there shall be no election of either of said officers, the legislature shall proceed to fill such vacancies in the manner provided in the constitution for the choice of such officers.

ties.note: Constitution of Massachusetts, Amendments Arts. XIV and XVI (as printed on the General Court's page, with superseded text in brackets). A tie is not named: that an exact tie is a case of 'no election' that goes to the legislature is a reading, and the manner of choice the Constitution provides in the original text (a ballot among the highest candidates) is among the bracketed, amended text; not relied on.

ties.steps: if a majority of the whole number of electors has not been chosen, the governor calls the general court together by proclamation and the senators and representatives assembled in joint convention choose by ballot electors to complete the full number
ties.who: the general court in joint convention

sources.quote: If, upon examination of the copies of the records of votes for presidential electors, it appears that a majority of the whole number of electors has not been chosen, the governor shall forthwith, by proclamation, call together the general court; and the senators and representatives assembled in joint convention shall by ballot choose electors to complete the full number.

ties.note: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 138. The section applies when a majority of electors is not chosen; a tie in the electors' vote is not named, and the reading that a tie for the slate is such a case is an inference.

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes cast for such office or on such question
threshold.conditions: statewide recount (office or question voted on by all the voters of the commonwealth): a petition signed in the aggregate by at least 1,000 voters, filed with the state secretary by 5 p.m. on the fifteenth day after the election; void if the difference between the two leading candidates (or the affirmative and negative votes) is more than one half of one per cent
threshold.in_words: a statewide recount is ordered only if the two leading candidates (or yes and no) are within one half of one per cent of the votes cast, and only on a petition of at least 1,000 voters

who_may_request: at least 1,000 voters, in the aggregate, on a form furnished by the state secretary (certified by the registrars of each city and town)
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the section read

sources.quote: if it then appears that the difference in the number of votes cast for the two leading candidates for the office, or in the number of affirmative and negative votes on a question, for which recount is desired is more than one half of one per cent of the total number of votes cast for such office or on such question, the petitions for recount shall be void. If such difference in the votes so cast appears to be one half of one per cent or less of the total votes cast for such office or on such question, he shall forthwith order the clerk of each city and town of the commonwealth to transmit forthwith
shall be signed in the aggregate by at least one thousand voters

recounts.note: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 135 (statewide recounts). For a state primary the petition is submitted to the registrars by the third day, certified by the sixth and filed with the state secretary by the seventh day after the primary. The statewide recount covers U.S. Senator and every office filled by all the voters of the commonwealth.

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes cast for such office or nomination or on such question
threshold.conditions: district-wide recount (office filled by fewer than all the voters of the commonwealth, at a state election or primary): a petition signed by one-fourth the number of voters required to sign nomination papers for state primary candidates in the district; the difference between any candidate and the apparent winner (or between the affirmative and negative votes) must be not more than one-half of one per cent
threshold.in_words: a district-wide recount may be petitioned for by any candidate within one-half of one per cent of the apparent winner, on a petition of one-fourth the signatures a state primary candidate needs

who_may_request: voters, on a petition signed by one-fourth the number of voters required to sign nomination papers for state primary candidates in the district, in the same manner as for statewide recounts
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the section read

sources.quote: District-wide recounts in cases of offices to be filled or questions to be voted upon at state elections, except by all the voters of the commonwealth, may be requested in the same manner as state-wide recounts, except that the petition shall be signed by one-fourth the number of voters required to sign nomination papers for state primary candidates in the appropriate district
is not more than one-half of one per cent of the total number of votes cast for such office or nomination or on such question.

recounts.note: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 135 (district-wide recounts). The kinds follow "offices to be filled ... at state elections, except by all the voters of the commonwealth" (federal House seats, the legislature, district and county offices on the state ballot) and state primaries [inferred for each office named].

recounts.election: any election, primary or preliminary election

threshold.conditions: a petition of ten or more voters of the ward or town (fifty or more of a ward in Boston; ten or more of each precinct in a precinct town of more than 2,500 voters), filed with the city or town clerk by 5 p.m. on the tenth day after an election or the sixth day after a primary or preliminary election, accompanied by the written request of the candidate for whom the recount is conducted, stating a belief that the records are erroneous and that a recount will affect the nomination or election
threshold.in_words: any candidate may have the ballots of a ward, precinct or town recounted, whatever the margin, on a petition of ten or more voters stating a belief that the record is wrong and that a recount will affect the result

who_may_request: ten or more voters of the ward or town (precinct), with the candidate's written request
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the section read

sources.quote: A petition for a recount may be filed with the city or town clerk on or before five o'clock post meridian on the sixth day following a primary or preliminary election, or on or before five o'clock post meridian on the tenth day following an election, in a ward of a city or in a town, if ten or more voters of such ward or town

and that they believe a recount of the ballots cast in such ward, precinct or town will affect the nomination or election of one or more candidates voted for at such primary, preliminary election or election

recounts.note: M.G.L. c. 54, s. 135, first paragraph. There is no margin condition; the petition must state a belief that the recount will affect the result. The recount is by the registrars of voters of the city or town; with an electronic voting system it is by rescanning, or by hand if the petition says so (s. 135B). No automatic recount was found in sections 115, 116, 134, 135, 135B and 137 of chapter 54.

unread.what: who pays for a recount; city and town charters, chapter 43 and chapter 41 (city and town elections and their ties); the Constitution's text for the senate's and house's judging of elections

notes: Massachusetts's general-election statutes (chapter 54 ss. 140 to 142) use 'failure to choose' or 'failure to elect' and call a new election; the word tie appears only in chapter 53 s. 53 (primaries) of the sections read. Every general-election tie rule above is therefore [inferred] on that reading.

Massachusetts has no automatic recount in the sections read; recounts are on voters' petitions (ten voters in a ward or town, any margin; 1,000 voters statewide within one-half of one per cent; district-wide within one-half of one per cent).
